passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a novel cognitive enhancer on reaction times in healthy adults. A randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial was conducted with 120 participants aged 18‑35, divided equally into three groups: Control (placebo), Low Dose (5 mg), and High Dose (10 mg). After a 4‑week supplementation period, participants completed a computerized Stroop task, and mean reaction times (RT) were recorded. The study reported the following average RTs: Control 520 ms (SD 45 ms), Low Dose 495 ms (SD 50 ms), High Dose 460 ms (SD 40 ms). The investigators concluded that the enhancer produced a dose‑dependent improvement in cognitive processing speed.
stem: Based on the data presented, which group exhibited the fastest average reaction time?

options.D: All groups had the same reaction time

explanation: The High Dose group had the lowest mean reaction time (460 ms), indicating the fastest performance.
trap: Picking Low Dose because it also improved on Control, although High Dose (460 ms) was faster than Low Dose (495 ms).

stem: What is the main purpose of randomly assigning participants to the three groups?

options.A: To make the groups similar at the start on both measured and unmeasured characteristics, by chance
options.B: To keep participants unaware of which treatment they received
options.C: To guarantee that the groups have equal standard deviations
options.D: To ensure that the high-dose group shows the fastest reaction time

explanation: Correct: A) Random assignment balances known and unknown characteristics across groups on average. Why the others are wrong: B) Keeping participants unaware is blinding, a separate feature. C) Randomization does not control spread of outcomes. D) It does not determine the outcome.
trap: Confusing randomization with blinding; keeping participants unaware of their treatment is the double-blind feature, not the purpose of random assignment.

stem: What is the percent improvement in average reaction time from the Control group to the High Dose group?
explanation: Correct: B) (520 − 460)/520 × 100 = 11.5%, using the control mean as the reference. Why the others are wrong: A) 5.8% is about half the correct value and does not follow from these means. C) 10.4% does not follow from (520 − 460)/520. D) 13.0% divides the 60 ms difference by the High Dose mean (460) instead of the control mean.
trap: Dividing the 60 ms difference by the High Dose mean (460 ms), which gives 13.0%, instead of by the control mean (520 ms).

stem: Which of the following conclusions is NOT supported by the data presented?

options.A: The enhancer produces a dose‑dependent improvement in reaction time.
options.B: The high dose group achieved the fastest reaction times.
options.C: The Low Dose group had the largest standard deviation.
options.D: Placebo has no effect on reaction time.

explanation: Correct: D) The placebo group's mean RT of 520 ms has no pre-treatment or no-pill comparison, so the data cannot show that placebo had no effect. Why the others are wrong: A) Mean RT fell from 520 to 495 to 460 ms as dose increased, and the investigators concluded a dose-dependent improvement. B) High Dose had the lowest mean RT (460 ms). C) Low Dose had the largest SD (50 ms versus 45 and 40 ms).
trap: Reading the placebo group as a no-effect baseline, although without a pre-treatment or no-pill measurement the data cannot show that placebo had no effect.

stem: Which cognitive process does the Stroop task primarily assess?

options.A: Selective attention and inhibition of an automatic response (cognitive control)

explanation: In the Stroop task participants must suppress automatic word reading to name the ink color, engaging selective attention and inhibitory control, so RT reflects processing speed under interference.
trap: Choosing memory: the task does not require encoding or recall.
